layers.sms_hardware: SN76489-compatible PSG behind port $7F (tone periods, attenuation, noise control, LFSR).
layers.original_driver_behaviour: Sound-bank driver executed from CPU $4000: mailbox, arbitration, headers, streams, tempo, steal, fade, reset.
layers.documented_adapter_decisions: PC choices: update rate, clock, resampling, loop cut points, mixing, OGG/runtime delivery. Must stay labelled adapter.
layers.original_driver_behaviour_note: The driver, not the request name, defines behaviour.

driver_tick.detail: IRQ ROM $005E0 calls the driver every frame; when $D12D==0 (PAL) it calls again every fifth frame ($005EA..$005F6): 6 calls per 5 frames = 60/s. NTSC ($D12D==1) = one call per 60 Hz frame. In the repo harness 72 entries per 60 frames were counted.

claims.text: Header at ROM $0B8EB: 4 channels (tone0, tone1, tone2, noise), duration multiplier 1, tempo byte $1C (28), tone transposes -13/-13/-13, noise 0.
Playing alone, the driver reaches an exact RAM recurrence at update 803 with period 19768 updates (329.5 s at 60 updates/s); the next period's PSG byte stream is identical.

In the repo SMS frame harness the unattended ROM requests $90 at boot (driver tick 35). Replaying only the mailbox, pause and fade inputs (fade = DE09/DE0A/DE0B 12/1/2, ROM $18E1), the isolated driver emits PSG bytes identical to the game IRQ path for all 4559 captured ticks (includes 3 game fades and 44 requests).
Commands executed in 3000 updates: E0,E1,E7,F0,F5,F6,F7 (custom ADSR, detune, tie, vibrato/pitch-env, volume-envelope select, jump, repeat).
Music is not stopped by the driver at the end of the intro section: channels jump to loop targets and play indefinitely until a new request, fade or $F8.
The fade that ends the opening is a game-side direct fade (ROM $18E1), not a request ID; the POC must reproduce it as a fade adapter event.

claims.text: Header at ROM $0E376: one stream, latch $C0 (tone 2), stream CPU $A380, priority byte $38.
Occupies SFX slot $DF30 for 20 updates (active updates 1..20, inactive at 21), then clears priority DE0F.
Over $81 it flags music channel index 2 ($DEA0 bit 2) at the request update; the flag clears 20 updates later and the music channel is left silenced until its next note.
In-situ attract flow issues $BF 14 times over running music; each is reproduced byte-identically by the isolated driver (approximate harness).
Equal-priority requests are accepted: a second $BF or an $A6 restarts the SFX on the same slot.
Ring-counter wrap writes $A9 after $BF and replaces the pending mailbox byte (AUDIO-0).
